title: Frustration Tolerance Cards
goal: 24 short challenges that are a little frustrating on purpose: a tower that keeps falling, a knot that won't come right the first time, a game where someone breaks the rules. Each card comes with one move your kid practises while the frustration is really happening, in a small, safe dose, with you right there.
need: These cards, on your phone or printed and cut out
Things you already have: stones, cards, string, dice, a spoon
Ten minutes and a good mood, not a hard day

lesson.text: Frustration is easiest to practise in small doses, on a good day, when nothing big is at stake. Each card is a little frustrating on purpose, and each one ends with a move to try while the feeling is real. The move matters more than winning the challenge.
lesson.before: 'I don't get it! You're explaining it wrong!'
lesson.modelNote: The frustration was about not getting it yet, but it landed on the person helping. Once she noticed that, she could stop, breathe and start over, and the explaining could work.

academics.subject: Language
academics.text: saying a problem calmly, in words

academics.subject: Math
academics.text: luck, odds and keeping score fairly

academics.subject: Life skills
academics.text: staying in a hard moment instead of quitting

howTo.intro: The trap is rescuing them the second it gets hard. Pick a good day, do the cards with them, and let them see you get frustrated too, and use the move.

plan.what: Pick one card together, and read its move out loud.
Do the challenge, use the move when it gets hard, try again. 5 to 15 minutes.
Ask which move worked, and use its name on a real hard day.

troubleshoot.q: They blow up when someone breaks the rules
troubleshoot.a: Start with the That's not fair cards, and always warn them first that a rule will be broken. A break first, then the talk.

troubleshoot.q: They get rude with whoever is helping
troubleshoot.a: Name it calmly, once: 'That came out rude.' Then wait. Most kids can stop, breathe and start over once they notice it.
Make it smaller: three stones instead of five. Stop while it's still a little frustrating, before it turns into a fight.

skills.name: Frustration tolerance
skills.text: staying with something that isn't working yet

skills.name: Self-control
skills.text: a move ready before the feeling takes over

levelsLine: Three levels on every card. Explore: do it with a parent, using the move. Develop: add the Deeper part. Extend: redo it another day and say which move helped.

cards.name: Stone Tower
cards.t: Stack five stones until the tower stands on its own. When it falls: Hands off, then rebuild.
cards.d: Go for seven stones, or build it with your other hand.

cards.name: Card House
cards.t: Build a card house two floors high. When it keeps falling: Try another way. A wider base, or the cards at a new angle.
cards.d: Try for three floors, and count how many restarts it takes.

cards.name: Spoon Walk
cards.t: Carry a small potato on a spoon across the room. Drop it, and you go back to the start. When it wobbles: Slow breath, and keep going.
cards.d: Add a turn, or a step up and down.

cards.name: Domino Line
cards.t: Stand up 30 dominoes in a line, then tip the first one. When one falls too early: Slow breath, then set them up again.
cards.d: Add a curve, or a split into two lines.

cards.name: Balloon Keep-Up
cards.t: Keep a balloon off the floor for 30 taps in a row. When it touches down: Start over, from zero.
cards.d: Only your weaker hand, or only your head and knees.

cards.name: Other Hand
cards.t: Write your name neatly with your other hand. When it looks wobbly: Add yet. 'I can't do it yet.'
cards.d: Write a whole sentence, then compare it with your first try.

cards.name: New Knot
cards.t: Learn a new knot from a picture, with no help for five minutes. When it won't come right: Name it. 'I'm frustrated with this knot.' Then try again.
cards.d: Tie it again with your eyes closed.

cards.name: Tongue Twister
cards.t: Say 'red leather, yellow leather' five times fast. When your tongue trips: Add yet, and slow it down.
cards.d: Make up your own, and try it on the family.

cards.name: Show Me Again
cards.t: A parent shows a card trick or a puzzle once. Try it. When you're lost: Ask kindly. 'Can you show me again?'
cards.d: Learn it well enough to teach it back.

cards.name: Paper Toss
cards.t: Toss a crumpled paper ball into a bin from three big steps away, ten throws. When you keep missing: Try another way. Underhand, overhand, a higher arc.
cards.d: Throw with your other hand, or over your shoulder.

cards.name: The Long Wait
cards.t: Put a treat on the table and wait five minutes without touching it. When you want to grab it: Hands off.
cards.d: Wait ten minutes, then share it.

cards.name: Slow Race
cards.t: Race across the room. The slowest one wins, but you must keep moving. When you want to rush: Smaller step. The tiniest steps you can.
cards.d: Do it carrying a full cup of water.

cards.name: The Untangle
cards.t: Untangle a knotted string without yanking or cutting. When you want to yank: Take a break. Put it down for one minute.
cards.d: Untangle it with a partner, one hand each.

cards.name: Ten Pieces
cards.t: Find where ten puzzle pieces go, one at a time. When you're stuck: Try another way. Sort by colour, or by edges.
cards.d: Do it with the box picture turned over.

cards.name: Talking Turn
cards.t: Tell a story as a family, one sentence each. Wait until the person before you finishes. When you want to jump in: Hands off.
cards.d: Make the turns longer, and listen for one detail to use in yours.

cards.name: Rule Bender
cards.t: Play a simple game. A parent says first: 'This round, I'll break one rule.' When you catch it: Normal voice. 'Wait, that's not the rule.'
cards.d: Swap: you break one rule, and the parent catches it.

cards.name: Rule Spinner
cards.t: Halfway through a game, spin a spinner or roll a die to change one rule, like 'play with your other hand'. When the rule changes: Start over. 'Okay, new game.'
cards.d: Write your own list of six rule changes.

cards.name: The Wrecker
cards.t: Build a block tower together. A parent says first: 'At some point, I'll knock it over.' When it falls: Take a break, then come back.
cards.d: Rebuild it together, better than before.

cards.name: Bad Ref
cards.t: Play a game where one player is the ref and makes one wrong call, on purpose. When the call is wrong: Normal voice. Say it once, then let it go.
cards.d: Take turns being the bad ref.

cards.name: Unfair Shares
cards.t: A parent says first: 'I'm going to split these coins unfairly,' then does. When it's unfair: Normal voice. Say what's wrong, and suggest a fair split.
cards.d: Split them three ways, with a fair rule everyone agrees to.

cards.name: Head Start Race
cards.t: Race a parent who gets a big head start. You'll probably lose. When you lose: Good game. 'Good race. Again?'
cards.d: Shrink the head start until the race is close.

cards.name: Dice Duel
cards.t: Ten rounds: both roll, the highest roll wins the round. It's all luck. After every round: Good game.
cards.d: Play 30 rounds, keep score, and see how close it ends.

cards.name: Lose on Purpose
cards.t: Play a game and try to lose it on purpose, without the other player noticing. At the end: Good game, and mean it.
cards.d: Explain how you lost, and what that felt like.

cards.name: Cheer the Winner
cards.t: Play a quick game. Whoever loses gives the winner a pretend medal and one real compliment. When you lose: Good game.
cards.d: Name one thing you'll try differently next time.

reference.title: The 11 Moves
reference.intro: Every card ends with one of these moves, like 'When it falls: Hands off.' The challenge makes the frustration. The move is what your kid practises while they feel it. Read them together before you start, and use their names out loud.

items.name: Moves for your body

lines.v: hands in your lap, count to five, then try again
one slow breath in, a longer one out
walk away for a minute, then come back

items.ask: Which one does your body need first?

items.name: Moves for the task

lines.v: shrink it to the very next little bit
go back to the beginning, with no comment
same goal, a different way to get there

items.ask: Which one do you forget to try?

items.name: Words for yourself
items.ask: Which one could you say quietly, just to yourself?

items.name: Words for others

lines.v: say what's wrong at your usual volume

items.ask: Which one does someone in your family need most?

conclusion.headline: A little frustration doesn't knock them over anymore.
conclusion.text: Notice the first time they use a move without a card in front of them: a 'can you show me again?' instead of a rude answer, or a short walk away from a broken game. That's the practice paying off on a real day.
conclusion.celebrate: When they use a move in a real moment, name it: 'You took a break and came back. That's exactly the move, and you did it on your own.'
extensions: Let your kid invent a new frustration card for you to try
Pick a family move of the week, and use its name all week
Redo the hardest card in a month and see what changed
Turn one card into a family challenge night, grown-ups included

signs: They use a move's name on their own: 'I need to take a break'
They ask for help without being rude
They say a broken rule out loud, in a normal voice
makeItReal: The next time real frustration shows up, name the move instead of the problem: 'This is a Take a break moment.' Then do the move with them.

fromHome.text: My daughter gets frustrated when she doesn't get a math concept right away, or doesn't understand a passage in the book she's reading. She starts being rude to the person trying to explain, and she shuts down. When I help her realize she's being rude, she stops, breathes and starts over.
